title: SEBI Directs Intermediaries To Overhaul FATCA And CRS Reporting Under New Income-Tax Rules
meta_description: SEBI's 11 November 2026 circular tells Reporting Financial Institutions to align FATCA and CRS systems with the Income-tax Act, 2025.
court: Securities and Exchange Board of India
case_name: Due Diligence and Reporting Requirements under FATCA and CRS, read with the Income-tax Act, 2025 and Income-tax Rules, 2026
body: A SEBI-registered intermediary that holds accounts for non-resident clients has, for over a decade, had to identify which of those clients count as reportable persons under the FATCA arrangement with the United States and the OECD's Common Reporting Standard, and pass that information up the chain for automatic exchange with tax authorities abroad. On 11 November 2026, SEBI told intermediaries that the rulebook under which they do this has changed, and that their onboarding and KYC systems need to change with it.

The circular, numbered HO/38/14/(18)2026-MIRSD-POD2/I/25560/2026 and signed by Deputy General Manager Bhumika Kanojia, applies only to registered intermediaries that meet the definition of a Reporting Financial Institution under Rule 238(8) of the Income-tax Rules, 2026, not to every SEBI-registered entity by default. For those that do qualify, the circular restates their due diligence and reporting duty under Section 508 of the Income-tax Act, 2025, read with Rules 238 to 240, which replaced the older statutory basis for FATCA and CRS compliance that intermediaries had been working to.

What this means in practice is a KYC form that has to do more than confirm identity and address. Intermediaries are expected to capture a self-certification from the client that specifically addresses FATCA and CRS status, including, according to secondary commentary on the circular, a validity indicator and information on who controls an entity where the account holder is not an individual. Identity and address verification done under the ordinary securities KYC framework is necessary groundwork but does not by itself answer the FATCA and CRS questions the new rules require.

SEBI's circular does not operate in isolation. It points intermediaries to the Central Board of Direct Taxes' Guidance Note on FATCA and CRS dated 24 July 2026 for the detail of how the due diligence and reporting is meant to work, leaving the operational mechanics to that guidance rather than spelling them out afresh in the circular itself. The circular's own role is narrower: it is SEBI discharging its obligation, as sectoral regulator, to instruct the intermediaries it regulates to fall in line with the new Income-tax Rules framework.

Coverage of the circular diverges on one point that matters to any intermediary trying to plan its compliance timeline: whether a specific deadline has been set for updating KYC systems and self-certification formats. One account of the circular states plainly that it sets no deadline of its own for intermediaries to complete the changeover. Another suggests the circular itself represents the compliance deadline SEBI had flagged, without naming a date. Given that disagreement, and without sight of the circular's full text in this search, the safer statement is that intermediaries should treat the obligation as current rather than wait for a separately announced cut-off, until the circular's own text is checked.

The circular also appears not to prescribe a specific penalty or interest consequence for non-compliance, according to the commentary reviewed, which places the burden back on each intermediary's general regulatory exposure for KYC lapses rather than creating a standalone FATCA or CRS penalty under securities law. Responsibility for obtaining the certifications and reporting them correctly is stated to rest with the intermediary itself, not with any shared infrastructure acting on its behalf, such as a KYC Registration Agency that merely stores what the intermediary uploads to it.

For an NRI, a foreign national, or an entity with a foreign controlling person opening or maintaining a securities account in India, the practical change is procedural rather than substantive: the tax residency and FATCA or CRS questions on the account-opening form are not going away, and the circular signals that intermediaries are expected to have the back-end systems to capture, store and report that information correctly under the current statutory framework rather than one that has since been replaced. Account holders who assumed an older certification given years ago still covers them should expect their broker, depository participant or asset manager to come back with a fresh or updated self-certification request in the coming months.
why_it_matters: FATCA and CRS reporting is how Indian tax residency, bank and securities account information about non-residents gets shared automatically with tax authorities abroad, and vice versa for Indian residents with foreign accounts. This circular confirms that SEBI-regulated intermediaries are now expected to run that due diligence under the Income-tax Act, 2025 framework rather than the older one, which affects every NRI, OCI, foreign national and foreign-controlled entity holding a demat, trading or mutual fund account through an Indian intermediary.
card_summary: SEBI's 11 November 2026 circular directs intermediaries that qualify as Reporting Financial Institutions to align FATCA and CRS due diligence and reporting with the Income-tax Act, 2025 and new Rules.
card_tip: Holding a securities or mutual fund account in India as an NRI, OCI or foreign national, expect your intermediary to ask for a fresh FATCA and CRS self-certification under the new rules.
verification_notes: AUDIENCE: NRI / OCI / foreign national / foreign company with Indian securities holdings. TARGET QUERY: do NRIs need to redo FATCA CRS declarations with their Indian broker or demat account. DEMAND EVIDENCE: none seen; selected because the circular was independently reported within days by several compliance-focused outlets, suggesting active industry attention, not from a traffic or search-volume signal. The circular number, date (11 November 2026), its restriction to Reporting Financial Institutions under Rule 238(8), the statutory basis in Section 508 and Rules 238-240 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 and Income-tax Rules, 2026, the reference to the CBDT Guidance Note of 24 July 2026, and the signatory are each confirmed from at least two of TaxGuru, CorpLawUpdates, VisaVerge and Teamlease RegTech, which independently describe the same circular in consistent terms. Left out as unconfirmed, with sources disagreeing: whether the circular itself sets a specific compliance deadline, which this piece states is unsettled rather than asserting either way; also left out is any penalty provision specific to this circular, since the sources reviewed describe none, and the exact wording of the revised self-certification form, which was not reproduced in full in any source opened. The circular's own text on sebi.gov.in was not located and opened in this run; this item rests on secondary legal-update coverage rather than the primary circular.
